text:
jess: heads up — seeing a small but noisy cluster of clients in eu-west that hit a series of immediate reconnects after a server-initiated soft close (1001). spikes in route churn and duplicate token meter shows up in the billing console. any recent routing/timeout rollouts?

kai: ugh, saw a blip in canary earlier; we flipped region-weight fallback weights at ~1757999000 but nothing that should force closes. can you paste a sample log?

jess: snippet from edge-proxy logs: 
```
2025-06-05T12:07:10Z INFO conn=abcd close_sent=1001 reason="client_idle" route=v2-weighted fallback=eu-fallback
2025-06-05T12:07:10Z DEBUG conn=abcd proto=X-Stream-v2 ping_ms=150 last_recv=29s
```
The client then reconnects immediately, gets routed to a different shard, and we see duplicate metering for the same long-lived session (app-level tokens).

mike: ping_ms 150 and last_recv=29s look suspicious vs proxy idle threshold. Our proxy idle default is 30s for that pool. If client pings once every 30s exactly you can get off-by-one on close/wake.

kai: agreed. looks like a thin race: client heartbeat at 30s, proxy idle at 30s -> server thinks idle, sends soft close just before client's ping. client reconnects right away. when weight-rollout started we saw slightly higher latency so the jitter reduced and hit the race more often.

jess: makes sense. two asks: (1) can we avoid duplicate billing for quick reconnects? (2) can console telemetry show route_version so we can correlate churn to rollouts? right now billing metrics don't include route metadata and it's hard to prove correlation.

mike: for billing, we can add a short dedupe window server-side: if a session token reconnects within 5s of a soft-close, mark as resumed and don't bill again. low risk and obvious UX win. PR idea: add `reconnect_grace_s` config per-tenant with default 5s.

kai: that helps, but we should also stop the soft-close from happening when a client is borderline. quick mitigation: bump idle threshold to 35s in eu pool for canary for 1h and enable more detailed `conn-heartbeat` logs. I'll open a rollout.

jess: +1. about telemetry: tina can we add `route_version` and `route_weight` tags to the streaming ingress metric (stream.requests) and the billing meter so we can pivot? right now metrics are per-route-id only.

tina: yea we can add tags but note console cardinality concerns. propose we add sparse `route_version` as a tag only for dev/canary and as an attribute (not tag) for prod until we vet cardinality. we can also add a dashboard quick-query that joins telemetry with rollout events.

jess: that's perfect. short plan: (A) mike -> implement reconnect dedupe (5s default) and add feature flag, (B) kai -> bump eu idle to 35s for 1h and enable debug logs, (C) tina -> add route_version to canary metrics + dashboard query, (D) jess -> monitor billing/cost and revert if unexpected.

mike: starting the branch now. ps — will gate dedupe behind `stream.reconnect_dedupe` feature flag and add metric `stream.reconnect_dedupe.hits`.

deploy-bot: deploy queued for staging: mike/reconnect-dedupe -> staging at 1758002000.

kai: I'll patch the pool config and kick canary in 2m. will post canary link.

jess: thanks all. filing follow-up: if we still see >0.5% churn post mitigation we escalate to rollback weights. otherwise we'll keep the dedupe and telemetry as permanent changes. :thumbsup:

mike: quick note — adding unit test for dedupe edgecases (race when soft-close overlaps actual session end). will include test vectors.

tina: i'll add a console banner idea: when a rollout changes route weights >10% we show an optional "streaming impact" explanatory tooltip so ops knows to watch churn. low-traffic but helpful.

jess: sounds good. keeping this thread as the single source of truth for the next hour while we watch the metric. will update.
